## Hard-to-vary report: the Time Traveller's fourth-dimension argument

**What I am judging.** The document is a novel, and the method rules out taste, so I do not judge the prose. What it contains is an explanation, put forward by the Time Traveller and demonstrated before witnesses. That is what I test.

### 1. The question, frozen

The opening makes one matter central: he is "expounding a recondite matter", and what he controverts is "the geometry… they taught you at school." So:

**Is Time a fourth dimension of Space, and can a body be made to move along it — as the model appears to be?**

- **Range:** this room, this evening, this machine. The claim reaches every body and every time.
- **Compared with what:** the model sitting still on the table, and the earlier Thursdays when it was not visible anywhere.
- **Asked:** "What produces it?" (the lever produces the vanishing) *and* "What can we tell from what we see?" (the vanishing as evidence for the first). He runs the two together and reports the second as the first. That is the fault the rest of this follows from.

### 2. The parts, in his words

**P1** a mathematical line or plane has no real existence. **P2** any real body must have extension in four directions — Length, Breadth, Thickness, Duration. **P3** "There is no difference between Time and any of the three dimensions of Space except that our consciousness moves along it." **P4** gravitation limits up-and-down, so we are not free even in Space; balloons. **P5** the barometer trace is a line, therefore along the Time-Dimension. **P6** vivid recollection is "jumping back"; we are always getting away from the present moment. **P7** this lever sends it into the future, this one reverses. **P8** "diluted presentation" below the threshold — why we cannot see it. **P9** at speed the machine is attenuated and slips through matter; stopping jams it in, "possibly a far-reaching explosion".

**Jobs.** J1 why Time is thought different from Space (given — the Medical Man); J2 why we cannot move in Time (given); J3 why the model vanished (given — the demonstration); J4 why it was never seen on earlier Thursdays (given — the Psychologist, the narrator); J5 why we do not feel the drift (given, implied); J6 what tells this from a fourth *spatial* dimension (**added** by me); J7 what a bystander walking through the machine's space would see (**added** by me).

### 3. Part by part

| Part | Mark | Why |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | loose | swap "real" for any other required property; the argument is unchanged |
| P2 | borrowed | rests on a definition of "real body" that already contains duration |
| P3 | held if | held only by J1 — a doubt held by the room, not the world. It also pulls against P8 |
| P4 | held, by J2 | it blocks "we are free in Space"; idle for anything else |
| P5 | loose | the same reading in other words; the trace is at rest in its own frame |
| P6 | borrowed | rests on an unstated theory of memory |
| P7 | fixed | the owner set it. Both halves of a poke are named — but see the rig, below |
| P8 | loose, catch-all, no working gauge | it covers vanishing *and* staying |
| P9 | loose, and its prediction failed | he stops in a garden, unharmed |

I am not adding these up.

### 4. Whole-explanation checks

**Flip.** Had the model stayed on the table, P8 covers that too. So the single observation that does any work carries both outcomes. This is the sharpest finding.

**Direction.** A vanished model is read backwards into a cause. Right numbers, wrong direction.

**Answer in the starting points.** P2 and P3 put motion along time into the premise. "Time is only a kind of Space" is the conclusion under another name; P6 repeats it.

**Where the jobs came from.** J1–J5 are the owner's and his guests'. J6 and J7 are mine, so any part held only by them is *held if* those jobs are real.

**Pairs that pull.** (a) P3 against P8: the more the patch covers, the less the vanishing shows. (b) P9 against itself: pass through matter at speed, jam into it at zero. He then stops and does not jam, so the line is drawn in the wrong place.

**Catch-alls.** P8 is one. The Psychologist offers a gauge — a spinning spoke, a flying bullet — and it fails: both are blurred, not invisible.

**What the change list leaves out.** What happens to the table the machine stands on. Whether the machine drags its surroundings or cuts them. What a second observer sees. And the four new guests, who never saw the model at all.

**Rivals.** A conjuring trick — and the text names it, with its training ground: the Medical Man "had seen a similar thing at Tübingen", stresses the blown-out candle, and asks about "that ghost you showed us last Christmas". A fourth *spatial* dimension fits every change on the list equally. So does the model's destruction. Nothing on the list separates them.

**The rig.** The chairs are his patents, the table, lamp and candles are his, the room is his, the model is his, the seating is his — and he holds the Psychologist's hand in his own while the lever turns. The one change that would reach inside, opening the machine, is impossible by the claim's own terms: it is gone.

**Provenance.** P2 built — it sticks its neck out about every body. P4, P5, P8 asserted. The demonstration is fitted to a single evening, its conditions set by the claimant. The return — dust, the healed cut, the blood-stained socks — is asserted, and is a second route to the same job the argument does not need.

### 5. What would make it harder to vary

1. **Give P8 a gauge.** Name one thing a bystander could read while the machine is "below the threshold" — a weight on the table, a shadow, a draught — and say what reading would worry him. Or drop P8 and admit only that the model left the table, by some route.
2. **Repeat the demonstration in a rig the guests build,** with the machine tethered, watched without a break, and handed back afterwards, open.

### 6. What this does not show

Passing would not make it true, and failing does not make it false. A time machine may exist; this evening's argument does not hold one in place. Nothing here judges the book.

### 7. One next step

Put the change question to him: **"What would we have seen tonight if the machine had not gone?"** If the answer is "the same", P8 is doing all the work and the demonstration is worth nothing.
